claims.text: Intermediate thermal aging produces a transient ductile-brittle-ductile transition in FCC/B2 eutectic HEAs.
The transition is driven by percolation and subsequent disruption of ordered B2 domains through LCO and phase-boundary evolution.
The initial alloy contains fine, dispersed B2 precipitates.
The initial alloy has a high dislocation density.
There is an intermediate aging-temperature range in which LCO evolution is active while grain coarsening and impurity segregation are negligible.
Within this range, elemental diffusion permits ordering inside B2 domains and phase-boundary migration but not full phase decomposition or grain growth.
Intermediate aging increases the coherence and volume fraction of LCOs within the B2 phase.
Changes in ordered-domain morphology and volume fraction affect mechanical behavior.
B2 domains coalesce into a coherent, continuous network at FCC/B2 phase boundaries.
The continuous ordered network acts as a superlattice barrier that pins dislocations.
The ordered network suppresses dislocation cross-slip.
Dislocation blocking by the ordered B2 network causes brittle fracture.
At higher aging temperatures, thermal energy overcomes the ordering enthalpy and disorders or dissolves LCOs.
Alternatively, Ostwald ripening of B2 domains at higher temperature breaks the percolating network.
Disordering or loss of B2 connectivity permits dislocations to bypass the ordered domains and restores ductility.
Elongation to failure decreases as LCOs percolate and then increases sharply when LCOs disorder or phase boundaries coarsen beyond the critical threshold.
The lower boundary of embrittlement occurs when the LCO correlation length exceeds the inter-particle spacing and establishes percolation.
The upper boundary of embrittlement occurs when LCOs fully disorder or B2 domains coarsen significantly.
Direct experimental data on LCO-evolution kinetics are lacking for the specific FCC/B2 alloy system.
A ductility minimum before network percolation, or ductility recovery without reduced LCO ordering or B2 connectivity, would falsify the proposed mechanism.
